answer: An agent economy weights each identity solely by the count of DISTINCT outside graders who have countersigned its trailing-window record. Honest graders form a fixed karst of some 50 springs. At settlement the ledger recounts distinct signers per key and zeroes any weight drawn from shared or kin-correlated signatures. Twelve hundred clones must dip into that one karst, so the 51st endorsement finds no unused spring and the marginal cost of each identity rises with n. Every signature is a slow shale layer laid down across a single voyage, non-poolable and impossible to pre-age in parallel.
